key_insight: This paper introduces autoregressive Boltzmann Generators, a more flexible way to sample equilibrium molecular states than standard normalizing-flow-based BGs. The key idea is to preserve exact likelihoods while relaxing the expressivity limits of strict invertibility.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of efficiently generating uncorrelated equilibrium samples for molecular systems, a core challenge in statistical physics and molecular simulation. Existing Boltzmann Generators often rely on normalizing flows that can be too restrictive, limiting how well they capture complex energy landscapes.
method: Uses an autoregressive generative model to improve expressivity over traditional invertible flow architectures.
Retains exact likelihood evaluation, enabling principled training and sampling.
Combines generation with importance sampling correction to produce equilibrium samples efficiently.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this expands the design space for generative models used in scientific computing, especially where physical validity and exact probabilities matter. It can improve sampling efficiency in molecular modeling and related simulation-heavy domains.
